## Guiana Amazonian Park — the largest park in French Guiana

### Guiana Amazonian National Park!

Guiana Amazonian National Park is France's largest national park and is located in French Guiana. It covers 33,900 square kilometers and was established on February 27, 2007. No roads lead into the park: it can only be reached by air or by water.

Much of the park is under special protection, with all mineral extraction prohibited in this zone. There is a reason for this restriction: gold can still be found relatively easily in the beds of the park's rivers. The rest of the national park is allocated to local Indigenous communities: the Wayana, Teko, and Maripasoula peoples.

### The rich natural world of Guiana Amazonia!

The entire park lies within the tropical rainforest zone. Guiana Amazonia is home to approximately 5,800 plant species, including more than 1,200 tree species, 85 types of palms, over 300 fern species, and several hundred varieties of orchids. Its wildlife is equally diverse: around 480 species of freshwater fish, just over 180 mammal species, nearly 300 species of reptiles and amphibians, and approximately 720 bird species. Turtles, snakes, and frogs are especially abundant, while local alligators stand out among them. Beautiful butterflies account for a striking share of the park's insect life.

Hacha forms a wide curtain of water above Canaima Lagoon. It is easy to admire from a boat: waterfalls rise beyond the dark water, framed by a green shoreline. Up close, the roar of the cascade becomes part of the experience.

A visit to Hacha is often combined with Sapo Falls. Guides decide how close visitors can approach the water and whether passage behind the cascade is possible, taking the weather and river level into account.

At Coloma, coffee grows among flowers and tall trees. You can linger over the red cherries on the branches, look for orchids in the garden, and spend time near the old house with its tiled roof. A trip from Bogotá leads to the warm, green surroundings of Fusagasugá, where you begin discovering one of Colombia's defining traditions.

The coffee tour follows the bean's entire journey, from the nursery and Arabica plantings to pulping, drying, and roasting. A guide explains how each processing stage affects the flavor of the finished drink. After the walk, tasting the coffee is particularly rewarding when you know what happened to the beans before they reached your cup. The hacienda's architecture and garden also make this stop appealing to visitors who usually choose coffee by a familiar brand alone.

On Ada Tours' coffee itinerary, a visit to Coloma occupies a dedicated day departing from Bogotá. It is a chance to experience rural Colombia without flying to another region. The estate also offers additional rum-related programs; participation and tastings depend on the specific itinerary. An independent visit and an organized excursion may differ in what is included.

Hacienda Venecia is located in the countryside near Manizales, in Colombia's coffee-growing region. It is a working farm where visitors learn how coffee is grown, harvested, and processed. The plantations and traditional houses offer a look at coffee production in its natural setting, far from a city coffee shop.

The story continues with tastings and an introduction to different brewing methods. Visitors compare the drink's aromas and flavors and learn about coffee varieties and bean quality. The farm appeals to anyone who wants to understand the journey of Colombian coffee from start to finish and enjoy the rural landscapes of the coffee region.

## Jacó — a town with fantastic beaches!

Despite its relatively small size, Jacó has plenty to offer beyond its numerous bars, cafés, and nightclubs. Its many attractions are sure to interest travelers. The town's main draw is its beaches, which stretch along the entire town and continue far beyond it.

## Jacó — an ideal place for surfing and fishing

This small resort town is about a two-hour drive from San José. With abundant sunshine and greenery, warm water, and rolling surf, it is a popular surfing destination and has ideal natural conditions for fishing.

## Jacó — a gateway to national parks!

From Jacó, you can take an excursion to the Caño Negro wildlife refuge or visit the famous Turtle Island. The town also has plenty of market stalls, shops, bars, restaurants, and other entertainment venues.
